newsitem.title: UK: Marine safety group Silvertech plans AIM float.
newsitem.headline: Marine safety group Silvertech plans AIM float.

text.p: Industrial and marine controls group Silvertech International Plc said on Monday it planned to float on the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market in the autumn.
The group said it hoped raise around five million stg and would use the proceeds to increase the marketing of its Unified Control System (UCS) product.
UCS provides integrated control and safety systems solutions for offshore oil and gas platforms and floating production vessels.

Silvertech was founded in 1984 by three engineers Gordon Elliot (chief executive), Joe Quinn (technical director) and Ken Simpson (sales) who own about 75 percent of the group. 3I Group holds a 15 percent stake which it bought three years ago.
The group, which is expected to be valued at around 18 million stg, achieved turnover of 13 million stg in the year to January 31 1997, up from nine million stg in the previous year.

Silvertech said 65 percent of turnover in 1997 came from the petrochemical-based clients which include British Petroleum Plc, Shell Transport and Trading Plc, British Gas Plc and the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company.
Its non oil and gas-based customers include General Electric Co, Hoechst, the UK Atomic Energy Authority and Eastman Kodak Co
John East & Partners and Burrough Johnstone have been appointed nominated advisers and nominated brokers respectively.
